Results.ReviewText: I've been a Weber charcoal kettle guy forever, but my wife wanted a gas grill, so we have the Spirit II E-310 now. We selected this grill for its simplicity of design and small size. We didn't want a large grill taking up a lot of space on our deck, and the 310 fits the bill perfectly. Great Weber quality of finish. We ordered this grill from Ace Hardware, who assembled, delivered and set up the grill for us. The guys from Twins Ace Hardware in Fairfax VA did a great job, and even walked us thru the operation of the grill. While I'm still learning how to balance the gas elements' heat (vs charcoal cooking), so far everything we've grilled has turned out very well. Cleaning the grill is easy. Overall I am very pleased with our E-310.
Results.Title: Spirit II E-310 is a winner

Results.ReviewText:
After seven years and two tries at grilling with another well-known brand (no names, but it rhymes with 'mar foil') I finally took the plunge and spent the extra money on a Weber.

Oh. My. Goodness.

A couple of things I'd like to point out. First of all, our local Lowes has about 97 grills lined up outside for your consideration. There are several different brands out there on display...but no Webers. Those are all INSIDE where it's warm and dry. Now, why do you suppose that is? My theory is that they want to move the lesser product. Greater turnover, greater profit. Which is not a bad thing by any means, but having had two of those inferior grills (once again, no names, but it rhymes with harm oil) I can tell you plainly: if you get one of those based on price, you get what you pay for. Example: I can easily pick one of those things up with one hand, less the propane tank, of course. I'm sure they're NOT made of tin foil, but it sure does feel that way.

But the Weber! It's DIFFERENT.

Full disclosure: when I bought this behemoth in mid-June, I had the option of course to have it assembled and delivered. Had I taken that route, it might've been delivered by 4th of July. Maybe. As it happened, we were without a stove in our home at the time, so a cooker of some sort was pretty urgently needed. As such, I drove over to Lowes and picked it up in the box.

A big box.

A VERY big box. And heavy. About 120 pounds, if the specs are to be believed, and I do. And big? It just barely fit in the back of my little Nissan. But it did fit, and I did get it home, then I had to figure out how to get the darned thing OUT of my little Nissan! My sweetie and I are both older and arthritic, so this wasn't easy, but we did finally get it out of the back of the car and onto the ground. I didn't even try to carry it onto the veranda; instead, I opened the box and took it in piecemeal. Then I started the ever-dreaded assembly process.

But...surprise! It was easy. No swearing involved! The instructions are very well illustrated; just keep in mind that they apply to two different models of Spirit grills. If you remember this and read carefully you'll have no problems. There's even an app available that demonstrates things if you have issues, but I didn't have to take that route. Maybe two-three hours working slowly and deliberately and the job was done, and when finished my new Spirit II E-310 felt remarkably solid, unlike its tinfoil predecessors. It also felt heavy, but not at all bulky, and surprisingly maneuverable with its big plastic wheels. Just lift it from the left side and roll it around. 

Having accomplished this, it was time to mount the propane tank and fire it up for the first time. I love the fact that it's got a weight-based gauge on the side...it takes at least some of the guesswork out of the process. Just eyeball it and you'll know if you have enough fuel to finish your day's cooking tasks.

So. No more fooling around: turn on the gas, set the port side knob to ignite, and push the button, Max. 

POP! Off she goes. And boy howdy, does she go! I preheated the thing to 500 degrees in just a few minutes. I allowed it to burn off the manufacturing goo, then shut everything down for seasoning. A little olive oil cooking spray on the grates and away we went again. And in no time at all, it was burgers and hot dogs for everyone! YUMMERS!

Mind you, this is just our first go-round with Webbo (for everything must have a name, mustn't it?) but if it all goes as well as the first time, I imagine I will be enjoying this for a long time to come. After all, it comes with a ten year warranty, for heavens sake. Guess they mean for you to be using it for a while! I did invest in a cover, though it will be sitting on our screened-in veranda. Better safe than sorry. Besides, it looks...well, stealthily cool, under that black cloak.

Lesson learned: you really do get what you pay for. Spend a little bit more money on the front end and get yourself something that will last.
Results.Title: Third Time Lucky
